question: Should autoreview make the proposed Claude subscription and Bedrock models, effort levels, refusal fallback, provider-authentication isolation, and persistent run telemetry the default contract for existing users?
rationale: The branch changes established model selection, authorization routing, fallback cost and consent, configuration precedence, and local data retention; tests cannot determine the intended upgrade and product policy.

options.title: Keep new behavior opt-in
options.body: Preserve current defaults while exposing Bedrock, mixed authentication, fallback, and telemetry through explicit flags or environment settings with live proof.

options.title: Adopt the new defaults
options.body: Intentionally migrate existing users and document fresh-install, upgrade, fallback-consent, credential-isolation, retention, and deletion behavior with live evidence.

options.title: Split hardening from policy
options.body: Land narrowly proven credential and process isolation separately, then review defaults, fallback, and telemetry as smaller sponsored changes.

recommendation.title: Keep new behavior opt-in
recommendation.body: Preserve current defaults while exposing Bedrock, mixed authentication, fallback, and telemetry through explicit flags or environment settings with live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced and repeatedly maintained the current autoreview and panel behavior whose public contract would change.
